page: Amazon Web Services m6id.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by a dedicated 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor featuring 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading. Memory is configured with 128.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 with VNNI instructions, cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA-NI, and cache tiers including a 54 MB L3 cache.

Integrated local storage is a primary differentiator for the m6id generation, providing 1900 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD instance storage. Network performance includes a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The instance contains no hardware GPU accelerators, delegating all compute operations entirely to the x86_64 CPU cores and memory subsystem.

Benchmark evaluations position the m6id.8xlarge consistently within the middle 50% across most standard computational workloads. The system achieves a multi-core Geekbench score of 14,183.0 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 30,861.82. Memory bandwidth tests yield 149.49 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 68.14 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes. In real-world application benchmarks, it sustained 31.25 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 35.31 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Machine learning execution shows strong results on small models, attaining 270.9 tokens per second on 135M parameter text generation, but drops to the bottom 25% (6.14 tokens/sec) during prompt processing for large 70B models due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators.

By bundling high-capacity NVMe ephemeral storage with balanced CPU and DDR4 RAM, the m6id.8xlarge delivers qualitative operational cost efficiency for systems that benefit from low-latency scratch space or caching without paying separately for provisioned network block storage. It is suitable for database servers, intermediate data processing and ETL tasks, distributed caching, and backend web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m6id.8xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based instance equipped with a 16-core, 32-vCPU Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz, 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system includes 1900 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local instance storage and lacks dedicated GPUs. Benchmark scores align broadly within the median range across compute, memory bandwidth, and caching tests, delivering a multi-core Geekbench score of 14,183.0 and 31.25 million Redis SET operations per second. While small-parameter language model text generation achieves a top-quartile 270.9 tokens per second, large model execution is constrained by CPU-bound computation. The instance presents an efficient, balanced profile for relational databases, low-latency caching nodes, data transformation, and medium-scale web application serving that leverage fast direct-attached ephemeral storage.
